text:
pagerduty_bot: PAGERDUTY ALERT — P0: Cross-region steering anomaly detected (eu->apac).
pagerduty_bot: Symptoms: elevated 5xx from APAC customers, latency spike, route divergence observed in probes. Incident created: INC-2026-0421-01
sre_oncall_niko: on it. paging into #incidents and tagging netops. i'll join bridge in 60s. @maria_netops can you pull routing logs?
maria_netops: looking — early signal: at 02:14 UTC a steering-policy rollout (policy-id: sp-7861) was applied to prefix 10.88.0.0/14. that prefix overlaps with apac-customer-subnet mappings. seems the policy wrongly mapped region labels -> eu-west1.
maria_netops: dns logs show low TTL churn but we also have sticky pins for some client IPs. not all traffic moved, looks like subset hit new rule and got pinned to eu-west1.
deploy-bot: recent change: rollout sp-7861 merged in config repo by @eng_runtime 02:12 UTC. CI checks green. canary at ~5% started 02:13 UTC.
eng_runtime: fyi that change introduced a region-label normalization to handle legacy names. tests passed but didn't cover overlapping numeric prefixes.
lucas_prod: impact: ~12% of APAC requests saw 500s and latency from ~80ms -> 450ms. affected customers: handful of API keys with high APAC footprint. support already triaged two escalations.
karla_support: drafted customer note: "We're investigating an API routing disruption affecting some APAC traffic; short-term mitigation in progress, we'll update within 60 min." should we send now?
sre_oncall_niko: hold on comms until mitigation confirmed. mitigation plan: 1) revert sp-7861 canary -> stop rollout 2) pin traffic back to apac-primary for affected prefixes 3) monitor error rate. we'll do step 1 and 2 in parallel.
maria_netops: ok. for pin override i'm going to add a high-priority policy override that maps 10.88.0.0/14 -> apac-east1 with precedence 1000. applying now.
maria_netops: applying override with our controller:
```
POST /api/v1/steer/overrides
{
  "prefix": "10.88.0.0/14",
  "target_region": "apac-east1",
  "precedence": 1000,
  "reason": "emergency pin to mitigate misapplied rollout"
}
```
maria_netops: override pushed at 02:20 UTC. controller responded 200. propagation to edge proxies starting.
observability_bot: Telemetry update (02:22 UTC): 5xx rate for APAC decreased from 11.8% -> 3.2% over last 2 mins. RTT p95 for APAC falling from 450ms -> 120ms.
sre_oncall_niko: good. i'm stopping the sp-7861 rollout now (canary rollback):
```
kubectl -n infra exec deploy/steer-controller -- rollback --policy sp-7861 --to-revision 0
```
sre_oncall_niko: rollback executed 02:23 UTC, controller reports canary aborted.
deploy-bot: rollback job completed; rollout stopped. logs: "canary aborted due to manual rollback request"
lucas_prod: monitoring dashboards show error rate trending down. still seeing small tail of errors likely from pinned clients. i'll add a targeted KV cache flush for affected prefixes.
eng_runtime: recommendation: add a short-lived routing rule that forces clients with header X-Region-Hint: apac -> apac-backend as an extra safety net. i'll file a followup PR with test coverage for overlapping prefixes.
karla_support: sending customer update now (02:28 UTC): "Mitigation applied — traffic routed back to APAC. We're monitoring and will follow up once fully stable. If you still see issues, please reply here with a request id. — Redwood SRE"
observability_bot: 02:30 UTC metrics: APAC 5xx down to 0.8%; p95 RTT 95ms. global error budget unaffected. no other regions impacted.
maria_netops: note for RCA: root cause appears to be label normalization mapping legacy label 'asia' -> 'eu' due to ambiguous mapping table; when policy matched, the prefix overlap caused misclassification. also automation didn't prevent precedence tie because canary applied precedence 50 which was lower than some sticky pins but higher than fallback rules, creating inconsistency.
sre_oncall_niko: creating incident timeline and assigning RCA to @eng_runtime + @maria_netops. severity: P0 -> Mitigated. oncall handoff: i'll remain until 03:00 UTC then hand to followup oncall @eng_runtime.
lucas_prod: raising one post-incident task: ensure canary rollout safety includes prefix overlap guard and explicit precedence tests. adding to eng-runtime backlog.
karla_support: will send consolidated customer update once RCA draft is ready. suggested template attached.
sre_oncall_niko: closing incident channel in 30m unless new alerts. great job team. :tada:
